title: Incoming Senate Oversight Chair Demands Corey Lewandowski Preserve DHS Records Ahead of Probe
snippet: Sen. Maggie Hassan has issued a warning to former DHS adviser Corey Lewandowski to preserve all records from his time at the agency as Senate Democrats prepare to launch a probe into corruption and waste.
content:
WASHINGTON — Sen. Maggie Hassan, the incoming chairwoman of the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee (HSGAC), has formally warned former Department of Homeland Security adviser Corey Lewandowski to preserve all records connected to his tenure at the agency, signaling a major congressional probe on the horizon.

In a letter sent Tuesday, the New Hampshire Democrat informed the high-profile Trump ally that the committee intends to use its full authority—including subpoena power—to investigate his actions at DHS, where sources say he functioned as a de facto chief of staff for former Secretary Kristi Noem.

A Scrutinized Tenure

"As incoming HSGAC Chair, I intend to use the Committee’s full authorities—including where necessary compulsory process—to expose corruption and waste. I therefore renew my request that you preserve all relevant records," Hassan wrote in the letter. "Should any such records prove unavailable when the Committee requests them, the Committee will want to understand how, and when, that came to be."

The congressional push follows news that Justice Department prosecutors have begun scrutinizing DHS contracting practices during the first year of the second Trump administration. That federal inquiry, which remains in its early stages, stemmed from an IG referral submitted by DHS Inspector General Joseph Cuffari regarding Lewandowski's conduct.

Under Oath and On the Record

Lewandowski has repeatedly denied any wrongdoing. Following reports of the DOJ inquiry, his attorney stated publicly that Lewandowski had not been contacted by federal prosecutors and emphasized that he "proudly serv[ed] his country in a voluntary capacity."

When Hassan previously requested that Lewandowski retain his records back in June—when Democrats held the minority on the committee—his legal team brushed off the request, asserting there was "no legal obligation" to comply.

However, Hassan used Lewandowski's own recent public statements to bolster her latest demand. Referencing comments he made on talk radio claiming he had "nothing to hide" and was "happy to have any conversations," Hassan made clear she intends to hold him to that promise.

"I look forward to having those conversations, on the record, under oath," Hassan wrote.

Attorneys for Lewandowski did not immediately respond to requests for comment regarding Tuesday's letter.
